extracted.intended_audience: research teams (principal applicants and co-applicants) preparing HFSP Research Grant (Early Career or Program) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for teams applying to the Human Frontier Science Program Research Grants (Early Career and Program), emphasizing novel, interdisciplinary, international basic research in the life sciences. Covers eligibility, team composition, scope, review process, and financial/administrative rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scope – innovative basic research into fundamental biological problems
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP Research Grants support innovative basic research into fundamental biological problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear emphasis is placed on novel collaborations that bring biologists together to focus on problems at the frontier of the life sciences. See guidelines for further scope details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on novel and interdisciplinary approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is given to novel and interdisciplinary approaches that involve scientific exchanges across national and disciplinary boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation of scientists from disciplines outside traditional life sciences (biophysics, chemistry, computational biology, computer science, engineering, mathematics, nanoscience, physics, etc.) is recommended because such collaborations open new approaches to complex biological problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internationality / intercontinentality of the team
rubrics_metrics.description: Research grants are provided for teams of scientists who are based in different countries and wish to combine expertise in innovative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams must be international (preferably intercontinental). HFSP expects international interactions to create new interfaces between scientific cultures; all-European or North American teams are rare and assessed critically. Teams with two members at the same institution are not eligible normally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team size and composition (2–4 members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants provide three years' support for 2–4 member teams; amount paid depends only on team composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of team members normally should be 2–4. Two members from the same country are acceptable if the team convinces reviewers that both are essential. In teams with members from for-profit institutions special rules apply (see financial rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Team members must be independent group leaders with a doctoral degree
rubrics_metrics.description: All team members are expected to direct a research group (however small) and must have a doctoral degree (PhD, MD or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must be in a position to initiate and direct their own independent lines of research. The HFSP award is not intended to create scientific independence; that decision must have been taken by the research institute prior to application. Written confirmation may be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Applicant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The research team must designate one Principal Applicant who is responsible for final submission of the Letter of Intent; the Principal Applicant must have their primary laboratory in an HFSP member country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Principal Applicant should be the person who will coordinate and drive the collaboration, keep the group together and oversee the entire project. Up to LOI submission the team can change the Principal Applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: independence and freedom to administer grant
rubrics_metrics.description: All team members must be able to determine the course of the HFSP-funded project and have freedom to administer the grant if awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP may request written confirmation from heads of department if there is doubt about an applicant's independence or freedom to administer funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Career grant eligibility windows
rubrics_metrics.description: For Research Grants – Early Career all members must be within 5 years of obtaining an independent position and have obtained their first doctoral degree not longer than 10 years before the LOI deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP considers periods of parental leave, compulsory military service, or major medical conditions for extensions—such periods must be included in the CV. Teams that do not qualify will be moved to the Program Grants competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preliminary results required
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary results are not required; applicants are expected to develop new lines of research through the collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP understands that frontier work is exploratory; however teams are expected to present convincing plans and mitigation strategies for risk rather than vague hopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: High risk–high reward expectation and risk mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP expects 'high risk - high reward' projects: bold aims that, if successful, would make a major contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hand-waving statement that a project 'may or may not work' is insufficient. Teams must explain why there is a reasonable chance of success, discuss limiting parameters of techniques, propose novel methods, and present 'plan B' approaches and mitigation strategies if key elements fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity: substantive, not token
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinarity normally means collaboration of biologists with scientists from other disciplines (chemistry, physics, mathematics, nanoscience, psychology, engineering, etc.), or teams combining very different expertise and scientific approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel combinations are required; use of 'off the shelf' tools or routine combinations (e.g., confocal imaging, routine bioinformatics) will not be scored highly. Adding a theoretician or member solely to appear interdisciplinary without defined methods and contributions is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team integration and proposed interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers pay particular attention to the proposed interactions between team members and the degree of team integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select each team member for their own expertise and expected specific contribution. Avoid adding partners for geographical location or prestige. Teams must convince reviewers of close collaboration of the entire team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that project represents new lines of research (not direct extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The project must be significantly different from applicants' ongoing research and not an obvious next step in their laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that are direct continuations or extensions of current work, or represent only incremental advancement using standard approaches, are unlikely to be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on prior collaborations / joint publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members should not have collaborated before and will normally not have published original research together; joint publications are used as a measure of joint work and may be seen critically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams that have joint publications (especially recent ones) should explain why those publications should not be considered; number, recency, and field relevance of joint publications are factors reviewers consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercontinental collaborations valued; regional teams scrutinized
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP expects international interactions and prefers intercontinental teams; purely regional collaborations (all-European or North American) are rare among successful proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such collaborations will be assessed on their merits; diversity in scientific cultures is seen as positive and can contribute to frontier-style innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: What HFSP does not fund – topic exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP does not fund projects of a purely applied nature (clinical/pharmaceutical focus, drug design/development), applied engineering/biotech/nanotechnology, development of methods not addressing basic biological questions, projects focused on agricultural/forestry/environmental/conservation problems, or purely observational/descriptive projects (large-scale screening, data collection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that are obvious next steps or incremental will be eliminated even if scientifically excellent; applicants should verify fit with HFSP priorities before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid purely observational/descriptive or large-scale collection projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Purely observational or descriptive projects, including systematic screening approaches and data-collection studies (e.g., on genomes, transcriptomes, connectomes, populations, ecosystems) are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP funds mechanistic, hypothesis-driven frontier basic research rather than large descriptive datasets unless clearly addressing a fundamental biological question in an innovative way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of field-country team member must be full integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding a team member from a country where field work is to be performed is supported only if that member is fully integrated into the team, not merely a 'field assistant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full integration means substantive intellectual and experimental contribution to the project, not token inclusion to justify field access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent application restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: No team member may be a Principal Applicant or Co-Applicant on another HFSP proposal; failure to ensure this will result in withdrawal of all those applications from the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal Applicant must ensure team members are not on other concurrent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial rules – award amounts and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are fixed sums dependent on team size; no detailed budget is required. The award is for costs specifically linked to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible costs include salaries or stipends for research assistants (post-docs, graduate students, technicians) essential for the new collaborative project. No salary support may be paid from the grant for the Principal Applicant, Co-Applicant, other faculty, institutional staff (secretaries, lab managers), and no student tuition fees can be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: For‑profit institution participation and award calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a two-member team includes one member in a for-profit institution, the annual award will be halved. In teams with more members, the for-profit team member will not be included when calculating the amount of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial calculations are made after scientific review and recommendation, and will take moves by team members after application into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two members from same country counted as 1.5 for award calculation when interdisciplinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Two members from the same country will be considered as 1.5 team members if they constitute an interdisciplinary collaboration, for the purpose of calculating award amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects the fixed-sum award amount; scientific review considers the team composition first, and financial adjustments are made afterwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process structure and evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed in two stages: LOI pre-screening for eligibility and scope, then full proposals by invited teams. Evaluation criteria include novelty, interdisciplinarity, and team integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LOIs are pre-screened by a small scientific committee for eligibility and concordance with scope; remaining LOIs are scored in detail by Review Committee members for novelty, interdisciplinarity and team integration. Selection Committee invites about 80–90 teams to submit full proposals. Full proposals are reviewed by at least two Review Committee members and external reviewers (aiming for at least three independent external reviews). The same criteria used for LOIs apply to full proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: DORA-based assessment of publications (content over JIF)
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP is a signatory to DORA: reviewers should evaluate research proposals on the basis of content, not solely by Journal Impact Factors (JIF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are advised to consider the quality of research published/proposed and the influence of candidates' publications in advancing knowledge, rather than relying on JIF.

rubrics_metrics.name: What makes a good research team (summary guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good teams demonstrate strong, well-justified interdisciplinary interactions, select members for specific expertise and expected contributions, and avoid token additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity in teams is positive. Teams should avoid adding partners for prestige or geography. Teams should convincingly describe planned close collaboration of all members and the specific contributions each brings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'independent position' and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent position is one where the applicant can determine the course of the HFSP-funded project and has freedom to administer the grant; theoreticians or computational biologists without conventional labs may still be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP recognizes non‑traditional group leaders and may request clarification; contact HFSP if in doubt, and HFSP may ask for written confirmation from heads of department.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI timing and mandatory steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must initiate and obtain an LOI ID and submit a Letter of Intent by specified deadlines (initiate by mid-March, submit LOI by end-March), and all co-applicants must approve participation via the online form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No changes can be made to the LOI after final submission. The Principal Applicant should obtain the LOI ID as early as possible. Selected LOIs will be notified by mid-July and invited to submit full proposals due mid-September (dates updated annually).
